title: Understanding substance use and health
content: Substance-use problems can affect physical health, mental well-being, relationships, education, work, and finances. Effects vary by substance, amount, frequency, route of use, other medicines, and individual health. Diagnosis and treatment planning require assessment by a qualified health professional. People should be treated with dignity and without stigma.
review_status: Starter summary; review relevant sections before public deployment

title: Finding de-addiction support in India
content: India's National De-addiction Helpline is 14446. The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment describes it as providing primary counselling and immediate referral services for people seeking help. Check the official government programme page for current service details. This information directory is not a substitute for an assessment by a qualified professional.
source_name: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment — NAPDDR
review_status: Official government source; re-check contact details periodically

title: Mental-health support in India
content: Tele-MANAS is India's national tele-mental health programme. Government health information lists 14416 for round-the-clock mental-health support. It can be a starting point for support and referral. If a person may act on thoughts of self-harm or is in immediate danger, call 112 or go to the nearest emergency department. Verify current service details on official sources.
source_name: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare — Tele-MANAS
review_status: Official programme source; re-check contact details periodically

title: Emergency response in India
content: India's Emergency Response Support System uses 112 as a unified emergency number. A suspected overdose, unconsciousness, difficulty breathing, seizure, or another potentially life-threatening condition requires urgent professional assessment. Do not wait for an AI response during an emergency. This application cannot diagnose or manage an overdose.
source_name: Ministry of Home Affairs — Emergency Response Support System
review_status: Official government source; review safety wording before public deployment

title: Reporting drug trafficking and illegal drug activity
content: The Government of India's MANAS National Narcotics Helpline uses 1933 for reporting drug-related matters such as illegal trafficking, illegal sale or purchase, storage, manufacturing and illicit cultivation. It is distinct from the 14446 de-addiction support helpline and is not a substitute for medical care or counselling.
source_name: National Portal of India — MANAS National Narcotics Helpline
review_status: Official government source; verify scope before public deployment

title: Treatment is individual and professional support matters
content: Substance-use treatment depends on the substance involved, the person's health, their circumstances, and clinical assessment. Recovery support may involve health professionals, counselling, structured treatment, peer or family support when appropriate, and follow-up care. Withdrawal risks differ among substances. Do not start, stop, or change medicines or attempt a detoxification plan based on an AI chat; consult a qualified professional.
review_status: General educational summary; clinical review needed before public deployment

title: Privacy and respectful support
content: A recovery-support application should collect only information needed for its purpose, explain what is stored, obtain clear consent before saving sensitive information, and avoid identifying users as having an addiction based on their questions. This prototype does not provide user accounts and does not intentionally persist conversations to a database.
review_status: Design requirement; privacy/legal review required before a real-user pilot

title: Tele-MANAS mental-health service
content: India's National Tele-Mental Health Programme provides 24x7 tele-mental-health support. The Directorate General of Health Services lists 14416 and 1800-89-14416. This service is not a replacement for emergency response when danger is immediate.
source_name: Directorate General of Health Services — National Mental Health Programme

title: Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan resources
content: The Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan is a Government of India initiative covering prevention, assessment, treatment, rehabilitation, aftercare, public information and community awareness. This project should complement existing services and must not claim that no public programme exists.
source_name: Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan official portal

title: eSanjeevani telemedicine resource
content: eSanjeevani is a Government of India telemedicine platform. Users should follow the official platform's instructions to see what consultation options are currently available. It is not an addiction-specific emergency service.
source_name: eSanjeevani — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
review_status: official platform; verify access options periodically

title: Emergency Response Support System 112
content: The Ministry of Home Affairs describes 112 as India's unified emergency response number. For immediate danger or life-threatening symptoms, users should contact emergency services directly rather than wait for an AI assistant.

title: Alcohol: what it is and how it affects health
content: Alcoholic drinks contain ethanol, a psychoactive and toxic substance that can cause dependence. Alcohol can impair judgement, coordination and reaction time in the short term; effects vary with amount consumed, drinking pattern, medicines, health, age and context. Alcohol use is associated with liver disease, cardiovascular harms, several cancers, injuries and mental-health conditions. The World Health Organization states that no level of alcohol consumption is entirely risk-free, while much of the harm comes from heavy episodic or sustained heavy drinking. Alcohol during pregnancy can harm fetal development. This summary is general health education, not an individual risk assessment. People who drink heavily or regularly and are considering stopping should discuss safe options with a qualified health professional because withdrawal can be medically dangerous for some people.
source_name: World Health Organization — Alcohol fact sheet (28 June 2024)
review_status: Summary of official WHO fact sheet; review with a qualified clinician before public deployment

title: Alcohol: signs of harmful use and support options
content: Possible signs that alcohol use is becoming harmful can include difficulty controlling drinking, strong urges to drink, continuing despite health or relationship problems, or neglecting important responsibilities. These signs are not a diagnosis by themselves. Treatment and support can include assessment by a qualified clinician, counselling and other evidence-based care depending on the person. Alcohol withdrawal can be dangerous, especially after heavy or prolonged use; an AI assistant should never provide a home detox schedule or tell someone to stop suddenly. In India, the National De-addiction Helpline is listed as 14446 for information/counselling/referral; verify current details on the official government page.
source_name: World Health Organization — Alcohol fact sheet and mhGAP guideline; India helpline information from Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
review_status: General educational summary; clinical and contact-detail review required

title: Tobacco and nicotine: health effects
content: All forms of tobacco use are harmful. Tobacco use increases the risk of cancer, cardiovascular disease, stroke and respiratory disease, and second-hand smoke can harm other people. Nicotine is addictive. The health risks vary by product and exposure, and this summary cannot assess an individual's health. A qualified health professional or an official tobacco-cessation programme can help a person explore quitting support.
source_name: World Health Organization — Tobacco and nicotine fact sheet
review_status: Summary of official WHO fact sheet; review periodically

title: Opioids: dependence and overdose warning signs
content: Opioids include substances such as morphine, tramadol, heroin and fentanyl. Non-medical use or use without medical supervision can cause dependence and other health problems. Opioid overdose can slow or stop breathing and can be fatal. Unconsciousness and difficulty breathing after possible opioid use require urgent emergency assistance; do not wait for an AI response. Medical treatment and effective support are available, and a qualified professional should guide treatment decisions.
source_name: World Health Organization — Opioid overdose fact sheet (29 August 2025)
review_status: Summary of official WHO fact sheet; emergency wording requires review

title: General substance-use disorder and recovery
content: Substance-use disorders involve patterns of substance use that can cause significant distress, health problems, or difficulty managing important parts of life. They are health conditions, not a reason to shame a person. The substance involved, pattern of use, physical and mental health, social context and personal goals all matter. Assessment and treatment planning should be individualised by qualified professionals. Recovery may involve health care, counselling, ongoing support and help with related mental-health or social needs. The assistant cannot diagnose a person or determine a single root cause from a chat.
source_name: World Health Organization — mhGAP guideline for mental, neurological and substance-use conditions
review_status: General educational summary; clinical review required before public deployment

title: Cannabis: effects on thinking, coordination and health
content: Cannabis is a group of psychoactive preparations from the Cannabis plant; THC is the main intoxicating component in many products. Acute effects can include changes in perception and mood, impaired memory and attention, and reduced coordination, which can make driving unsafe. Some people experience anxiety, panic or other distress. Frequent or prolonged use can lead to dependence in some users and may be associated with mental-health and respiratory problems, depending on the person and product. Effects and risks vary, and this summary cannot determine an individual’s health status. Consult a qualified health professional for personal concerns or treatment options.
source_name: World Health Organization — Cannabis information and technical brief (25 August 2026)
review_status: Summary of WHO material; clinician review required before public deployment

title: Psychoactive drugs: general health and support information
content: Psychoactive substances can affect perception, mood, cognition or behaviour. Different substances have different risks, effects and withdrawal patterns; they should not be treated as interchangeable. Use without medical supervision can cause health harms and some substances can produce dependence. A chatbot cannot identify an unknown substance, assess intoxication reliably, or provide a safe personal detox plan. For severe symptoms, suspected overdose, unconsciousness or difficulty breathing, seek emergency care immediately. For ongoing concerns, a qualified health professional can help assess the situation and discuss appropriate support.
source_name: World Health Organization — Psychoactive drugs overview and mhGAP guideline
review_status: General educational summary; review and expand with substance-specific guidance before public deployment
